cues.en: Let's talk about another kind of neural network, the Recurrent Neural Network.
cues.zh: 來談另一種神經網路：循環神經網路。

cues.en: What's a RNN for?
cues.zh: RNN 做什麼用？

cues.en: Well a couple of things.
cues.zh: 有幾種用途。

cues.en: Basically they're for sequences of data.
cues.zh: 基本上，用來處理資料序列。

cues.en: That might be a sequence in time, so, you might use it for processing time series data, where you're trying to look at a sequence of data points over time and predict the future behavior of something over time in turn.
cues.zh: 可能是時間序列，因此可處理隨時間出現的一連串資料點，再預測某個事物未來的行為。

cues.en: RNNs are fundamentally for sequential data of some sort.
cues.zh: RNN 基本上是處理某種循序資料。

cues.en: Some examples of time series data might be web logs where you are receiving different hits to your website over time, or sensor logs where you're getting different inputs from sensors from the Internet of Things,
cues.zh: 時間序列例子，包括持續記錄網站點擊的網頁日誌、物聯網感測器不斷傳入不同輸入的感測器日誌，

cues.en: or maybe you're trying to predict stock behavior by looking at historical stock trading information.
cues.zh: 或根據歷史股票交易資訊，預測股價行為。

cues.en: These are all potential applications for recurrent neural networks because they can take a look at the behavior over time, and try to take that behavior into account when it makes future projections.
cues.zh: 這些都是 RNN 的可能應用，因為它能觀察隨時間的行為，並將其納入未來預測。

cues.en: Another example might be if you're trying to develop a self-driving car.
cues.zh: 另一個例子，是開發自駕車。

cues.en: You might have a history of where your car has been, its past trajectories, and maybe that can inform how your car might want to turn in the future.
cues.zh: 可能有車子過去的位置與行駛軌跡，能幫助判斷未來該如何轉向。

cues.en: So, you might take into account the fact that your car has been turning along a curve to predict that perhaps it should continue to drive along a curve until the road straightens out.
cues.zh: 因此，可以考慮車子一直沿著彎道行駛，預測也許應持續沿彎道前進，直到道路變直。

cues.en: The sequence doesn't have to just be in time, it can be any kind of sequence of arbitrary length.
cues.zh: 序列不必只是時間，也可以是任何長度、任何種類的序列。

cues.en: Something else that comes to mind are languages.
cues.zh: 另一個想到的是語言。

cues.en: Sentences are just sequences of words, right?
cues.zh: 句子就是詞語的序列，對吧？

cues.en: So you can also apply RNNs to language, or machine translation, or producing captions for videos or images.
cues.zh: 所以，也能把 RNN 用於語言、機器翻譯，或替影片、影像產生說明文字。

cues.en: These are examples of where the order of words in a sentence might matter, and the structure of the sentence and how these words are put together could convey more meaning than you could get
cues.zh: 這些情況，句中詞序可能重要，句子結構與詞語組合方式，能傳達比

cues.en: by just looking at those words individually without context.
cues.zh: 單獨看每個詞、沒有上下文，更多的意義。

cues.en: So again, an RNN can make use of that ordering of the words and try to use that as part of its model.
cues.zh: 因此，RNN 能利用詞序，將它納入模型。

cues.en: Another interesting application of RNNs is machine generated music.
cues.zh: 另一個有趣應用，是機器生成音樂。

cues.en: You can also think of music sort of like text, where instead of a sequence of words or letters, you have a sequence of musical notes.
cues.zh: 音樂也能像文字，不是詞或字母序列，而是音符序列。

cues.en: You can actually build a neural network that can take an existing piece of music, and extend upon it by using a recurrent neural network to try to learn the patterns
cues.zh: 可以建立神經網路，接受既有音樂，透過 RNN 學習過去音樂中，

cues.en: that were aesthetically pleasing from the music in the past.
cues.zh: 美感上令人愉悅的模式，再延續它。

cues.en: Conceptually, this is what a single recurrent neuron looks like in terms of a model.
cues.zh: 概念上，單個循環神經元的模型，長這樣。

cues.en: It looks a lot like an artificial neuron that we've looked at before, the big difference is this little loop here going around it.
cues.zh: 很像之前的人工神經元，主要差異，是這個繞回來的小迴圈。

cues.en: As we run a training step on this neuron, some training data gets fed into it, or maybe this is an input from a previous layer in our neural network.
cues.zh: 對它執行訓練步驟時，傳入一些訓練資料，或是神經網路前一層的輸入。

cues.en: It will apply some sort of step function after summing all the inputs into it.
cues.zh: 輸入加總後，套用某種階躍函數。

cues.en: In this case, we're going to be using something more like a hyperbolic tangent, because mathematically we want to make sure that we preserve some of the information over time in a smooth manner.
cues.zh: 這裡會用比較像雙曲正切的函數，因為數學上，要確保能隨時間，平滑保留部分資訊。

cues.en: Now, usually we would just output the result of that summation and that activation function as the output of this neuron, but we're also going to feed that back into the same neuron,
cues.zh: 通常，把加總及激活函數結果，當成神經元輸出；但也會把它回送到同一個神經元，

cues.en: so the next time we run some data through this neuron, that data from the previous run also gets summed in to the results as an extra input.
cues.zh: 因此，下次資料通過時，前一次執行的資料，也會作為額外輸入，加進結果。

cues.en: So as we keep running this thing over and over again, we'll have some new data coming in that gets blended together with the output from the previous run through this neuron,
cues.zh: 不斷重複執行，新資料就會與神經元前一次的輸出混合，

cues.en: and it just keeps happening over and over and over again.
cues.zh: 一次又一次，持續發生。

cues.en: So you can see that over time the past behavior of this neuron influences its future behavior, and influences how it learns.
cues.zh: 因此，隨時間，過去的行為影響未來行為，也影響學習。

cues.en: Another way of thinking about this is by unrolling it in time.
cues.zh: 另一種思考方式，是沿時間展開。

cues.en: So what this diagram shows is the same single neuron just at three different time steps.
cues.zh: 這張圖，是同一個神經元，在三個不同時間步驟。

cues.en: When you start to dig into the mathematics of how RNNs work, this is a more useful way of thinking about it.
cues.zh: 深入 RNN 數學時，這種思考方式更有用。

cues.en: So if we consider this to be time step 0 at the left, you can see there's some sort of data input coming into this recurrent neuron and that will produce some sort of output after going through its activation function.
cues.zh: 如果左邊是時間步零，資料輸入這個循環神經元，通過激活函數後，產生輸出。

cues.en: That output also gets fed into the next time step, so if this is time step 1 in the middle with this same neuron, you can see that this neuron is receiving not only a new input,
cues.zh: 輸出也送入下一時間步，所以中間的時間步一，還是同一個神經元，不只接收新輸入，

cues.en: but also the output from the previous time step and those get summed together.
cues.zh: 也接收前一步輸出，再將兩者加總。

cues.en: The activation function gets applied to it, and that gets output as well.
cues.zh: 套用激活函數，再輸出。

cues.en: The output of that combination then gets fed onto the next time step, call this time step 2, where a new input for time step 2 gets fed into this neuron and the output from the previous step
cues.zh: 這個組合的輸出，再送到下一步，稱為時間步二，該步的新輸入送入神經元，前一步的輸出，

cues.en: also gets fed in, they get summed together, the activation function is run, and we have a new output.
cues.zh: 也送進來，兩者加總、執行激活函數，得到新輸出。

cues.en: This is called a memory cell because it does maintain memory of its previous outputs over time, and you can see that even though it's getting summed together at each time step, over time,
cues.zh: 這叫記憶單元，因為隨時間維持先前輸出的記憶；但也能看到，即使每一步都加總，隨時間，

cues.en: those earlier behaviors kind of get diluted, right?
cues.zh: 較早的行為會逐漸被稀釋，對吧？

cues.en: So we're adding in time step 0 to time step 1, and then the sum of those two things end up working into time step 2.
cues.zh: 因此，時間步零加入時間步一，兩者總和，再進入時間步二。

cues.en: So one property of memory cells is that more recent behavior tends to have more of an influence on the current time step.
cues.zh: 所以，記憶單元的一個特性，是較近期行為，通常對目前時間步影響較大。

cues.en: This can be a problem in some applications, but there are ways to work against that that we can talk about later.
cues.zh: 有些應用會有問題，但有方法對抗，稍後再談。

cues.en: Stepping this up, you can have a layer of recurrent neurons.
cues.zh: 再擴展，就能有一整層循環神經元。

cues.en: In this diagram, we are looking at four individual recurrent neurons that are working together as part of a layer.
cues.zh: 這張圖有四個個別循環神經元，作為同一層，一起運作。

cues.en: You can have some input going into this layer as a whole that gets fed into these four different recurrent neurons, and then the output of those neurons can then get fed back
cues.zh: 輸入整層後，送進四個不同循環神經元，再把它們的輸出，回送到

cues.en: to the next step to every neuron in that layer.
cues.zh: 下一步的該層每個神經元。

cues.en: So all we're doing is scaling this out horizontally, so instead of a single recurrent neuron we have a layer of four recurrent neurons where all of the output of those neurons
cues.zh: 只是水平擴展，不再只有單一循環神經元，而是四個組成一層，所有神經元輸出，

cues.en: is feeding in to the behavior of those neurons in the next learning step.
cues.zh: 都送入下一個學習步驟，影響這些神經元的行為。

cues.en: You can scale this out to have more than one neuron and learn more complicated patterns as a result.
cues.zh: 可以擴展到多個神經元，學習更複雜模式。

cues.en: RNNs open up a wide range of possibilities, because now we have the ability to deal not just with vectors of information or static snapshots of some sort of a state, we can also deal with sequences of data as well.
cues.zh: RNN 開啟廣泛可能，因為不只能處理資訊向量，或某種狀態的靜態快照，也能處理資料序列。

cues.en: There are four different combinations here that an RNN can deal with.
cues.zh: 這裡有四種 RNN 能處理的組合。

cues.en: We can deal with sequence to sequence neural networks.
cues.zh: 可以做序列到序列神經網路。

cues.en: If our input is a time series, or some sort of sequence of data, we can also have an output that is a time series, or some sequence of data as well.
cues.zh: 如果輸入是時間序列，或某種資料序列，輸出也可以是時間序列，或某種資料序列。

cues.en: So if you're trying to predict stock prices in the future based on historical trades, that might be an example of sequence to sequence topology.
cues.zh: 因此，根據歷史交易預測未來股價，可能是序列到序列拓樸的例子。

cues.en: We can also mix and match sequences with the older vector static states that we predicted just using multilayer perceptrons.
cues.zh: 也能將序列，與之前多層感知器預測的靜態向量狀態混合。

cues.en: We would call that sequence to vector.
cues.zh: 稱為序列到向量。

cues.en: If we were starting with a sequence of data, we could produce just a snapshot of some state as a result of analyzing that sequence.
cues.zh: 從一連串資料開始，分析後產生某種狀態的快照。

cues.en: An example might be looking at the sequence of words in a sentence to produce some idea of the sentiment that sentence conveys, and we'll actually look at that in an example shortly.
cues.zh: 例如，查看句子中的詞語序列，判斷它傳達的情緒，很快會看實例。

cues.en: You can go the other way around too.
cues.zh: 也能反過來。

cues.en: You can go from a vector to a sequence.
cues.zh: 從向量到序列。

cues.en: An example of that would be taking an image which is a static vector of information, and then producing a sequence from that vector.
cues.zh: 例如，接受作為靜態資訊向量的影像，再從向量產生序列。

cues.en: For example, words in a sentence creating a caption from an image.
cues.zh: 像是句子中的詞，從影像建立說明文字。

cues.en: We can chain these things together in interesting ways as well.
cues.zh: 也能用有趣方式，把這些東西串起來。

cues.en: We can have encoders and decoders built up that feed into each other.
cues.zh: 建立互相輸入的編碼器與解碼器。

cues.en: For example, we might start with a sequence of information from a sentence of some language, embody what that sentence means as some sort of a vector representation, and then turn that around into a new sequence
cues.zh: 例如，從某種語言句子的資訊序列開始，以某種向量表示句意，再轉成另一種語言的

cues.en: of words in some other language.
cues.zh: 新詞語序列。

cues.en: That might be how a machine translation system could work.
cues.zh: 這可能就是機器翻譯系統的運作方式。

cues.en: You might start with a sequence of words in French, build up a vector that embodies the meaning of that sentence, and then produce a new sequence of words in English or whatever language you want.
cues.zh: 從法文詞語序列開始，建立代表句意的向量，再產生英文或任何目標語言的新詞語序列。

cues.en: That's an example of using a recurrent neural network for machine translation.
cues.zh: 這是 RNN 機器翻譯的例子。

cues.en: There are lots of exciting possibilities here.
cues.zh: 有很多令人興奮的可能。
